title: Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1: triangle decompositions of typical graphs
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, "Counting designs" (arXiv:1504.02909): there are c₀ > 0 and n₀ such that every graph G on n ≥ n₀ vertices with all degrees even and 3 | e(G) that is (c,h)-typical, with density d(G) > n^(-10^-7) and c ≤ c₀·d(G)^(10^6), has a triangle decomposition; h = 2 (the paper's c-typical case, KeevashTri.theorem_2_1_ctyp, new in v2) and h = 16 (KeevashTri.theorem_2_1, v1). (c,h)-typical means |⋂_{x∈S} G(x)| = (1 ± |S|c)·d(G)^|S|·n for every vertex set S with |S| ≤ h; for h = 2 this is degrees (1 ± c)·d(G)·n and pair codegrees (1 ± 2c)·d(G)²·n (the paper asks (1 ± c) for pairs, so the hypothesis here is slightly weaker). The density and typicality thresholds are the paper's (n^(-10^-7) and c₀·d^(10^6)); c₀ and n₀ are not explicit. Quantitative internals of the c-typical proof: c_e = max(c, n^(-1/10)), goodness parameter c' = c_e^(1/4), at most η = 16c'^2·n + 4/(c'^2·d^16) bad one-vertex extensions of a c'-good set of at most 15 vertices. The proof follows the paper's strategy (random algebraic template over F₂^a, Nibble, Cover, Hole, Completion), with every random greedy algorithm of the Completion replaced by a deterministic potential (pessimistic-estimator) argument. Earlier registered entries are imported as lake dependencies: the hypergraph matching nibble of Ehard–Glock–Joos (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000004) and the Steiner triple system material of PALOMAR-2026-10-22-000017 v2. Mathlib does not contain this result.
